item.title: What we know about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Nvidia's board of directors on Monday said it has reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, less than two weeks after Huang resigned amid a scandal over an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. Yahoo finance senior reporter Brooke DiPalma, CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean and CBS News correspondent Natalie Brand have the latest.

item.title: Trump orders Army not to detonate unstable explosives in Iowa without court approval
item.description: President Trump said Monday he is ordering the Army not to carry out a planned detonation of unstable explosives in Iowa until it gets court approval. The planned detonation has been the subject of a court battle and community outcry over the risk of toxic lead particles spreading in a dust plume across parts of Iowa and Illinois.

item.title: Taking on credit card debt to buy food
item.description: This Thanksgiving, Americans are paying 32% more for food compared to what we paid in 2020. But according to a recent survey, about 63% of us are using credit cards to buy groceries – and many are having trouble paying off that food debt. Correspondent Lee Cowan looks at how rising costs, and the ease of Buy Now Pay Later apps, contribute to ever-tighter food budgets.

item.description: The princess reflects on her cancer journey in the documentary and speaks to others about their experiences.

item.title: Army delays detonation in Iowa that could send toxic dust into Illinois
item.description: The U.S. Army has delayed plans to detonate unstable explosives at a munition plant in Iowa, amid concerns about the risks of a plume of dust containing toxic lead particles that could spread across parts of Iowa and Illinois.
